programme.title: Children: Higher the Better
programme.desc: Join Kiteko, the goofy giraffe and Umi, the playful meerkat in Higher the Better, as they observe the everyday life of toddlers and learn from the children about their everyday activities such as picking apples and painting! When theyre not helping pick apples with the children, they are going on field trips and making lots of fun whilst they are playing. While watching, focus the attention of the youngster by speaking with them about what the children are drawing or how fast they can run! Combining education and fun, Higher the Better allows the development of social skills for toddlers, encourages them to observe and think deeper about what they are watching on their screen and initiates communication between parent and child, as well as children and their friends! Created by Ducktv, each animation, cartoon and mini-series is created with supervision of child psychologists to meet all the requirements of babies after three months of age. The combination between education, wholesome, amusing and relaxing elements within their shows aid toddlers to develop their visual and auditory abilities. Available 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, parents can be assured that their children can learn all the skills they need in life whilst still doing something fun!

programme.title: Children: Color Clara
programme.desc: Clara is an extraordinary, extra colourful, chameleon girl. Deep in the jungle in her cosy chameleon house, Clara uses her colour changing powers for good by helping her wrongly coloured jungles friends and objects to return to their natural colour. Making learning fun again, this exciting jungle tale helps young viewers to connect objects to their usual colours, developing their basic visual skills and introducing them to new and exotic environments such as the jungle.

programme.title: Children: Margo And Felix
programme.desc: Margo and Felix live in a beautiful little house which they must take care of themselves. Although they are responsible for the maintenance of the house they also make lots of time to play games and have fun. Taking on the activities of both adults and children helps to start communication between children and parents about responsibility. Margo and Felix encourages creative thinking and lots of fun!

programme.title: Children: Henrys Stories
programme.desc: Henry loves telling stories, but he needs your help to make sure its all in the correct order. Follow Henry in these silent animated shorts as he constructs stories with the help of his handy picture cards. Narrate the sequences together and solve his picture puzzles to see the story come to life. Identify the beginnings and endings of simple everyday stories, while carefully piecing together all of the events in between. Teaches children about cause and effect, while encouraging logical thinking and deductive reasoning.

programme.title: Children: Ducky and Friends
programme.desc: In Ducky and Friends our little duck is sharing all the fun with her friends, Lola, Henry and Toby. Stories are created with the help of child psychologists and aim to teach toddlers how to play nicely with their friends without arguing and how to adapt during mutual play. They also show that exploring the world with peers brings joy and satisfaction.

programme.title: Series: Cubie
programme.desc: Animated childrens series following Cubie the builder who has fantastic plans for new buildings. Cubie loves to build and, with help from his friends, the cheerful cubes, erects inventive new constructions. With Cubie at the helm, the cubes know exactly what to do, and if they encounter a problem, Cubie is always there to help. This enjoyable series from Duck TV helps children build their spatial awareness and observational skills while learning about new prepositions and the basics of building.

programme.title: Children: We Are Playing Now

programme.title: Series: Zack And Ziggy
programme.desc: This lovely animated childrens series explores the basic concepts of size and comparison. It follows the everyday adventures of a little nerdy boy named Zack and his loyal dog best friend, Ziggy. The inseparable pair turn every situation into a chance to learn, including taking a walk, playing sports and getting ready for bed. Join the two sweet friends on their exciting exploration of the world around them.

programme.title: Children: Risto Gusto
programme.desc: Lets have a look on Basils, Yams and Oreganos restaurant and peek out what goodies are made in the kitchen of Risto Gusto. There will be no question of what is healthy and what is unhealthy, because our favorites always offer the best for us.

programme.title: Series: Ristorante
programme.desc: Welcome to the Ristorante, come in and find out all about how the restaurant works. Learn about all the different processes starting with the preparation and moving to the baking or the cooking, the serving and finally to the dish washing. Encourage your little ones to play pretend, cooking up some imaginary treats for you, your friends and family. Come along to Ristorante and youre sure to build up your vocabulary, whilst improving your ability to identify basic objects and their characteristics, and of course having fun!

programme.title: Children: Sunville – Sportsville
programme.desc: All of your favourite Sunville residents join together to participate in one amazing sports day. Mister Goat, the Raccoon Family, Kitty Cat and the Friendly Pig are participating in Sports Day, and they want you to come along and join the fun! This interactive cartoon encourages children to join in and exercise alongside these incredibly cute characters, who can at times be a little competitive, too. In doing so, not only will your child have lots of fun, but they will be exercising and developing basic coordination skills along the way. They will also increase muscle strength and sense of balance, which will benefit them in their everyday lives, and keep them healthy and happy!

programme.title: Children: Lola and the Numbers
programme.desc: Lola is a playful little girls who loves numbers! She is constantly on the move and is always ready to count together with her number firends from one to ten. Lola and the Numbers is all about setting that pre-math knowledge for its young viewers. The show helps us to identify different numbers, count from one to ten and develop our pre-math skills. The most important viewing tip is that we always count with Lola! whether in English or your own language, counting along is always fun!

programme.title: Children: Sounds Around Us
programme.desc: Liza and Ben the little elf twins love learning about new sounds. Join them in this series of animated shorts to learn more about sounds, how to find them and how to recreate them. Follow them as they whizz away on exciting adventures together to investigate where different familiar sounds are coming from. Play along with the twins and encourage your child to listen and identify the sounds you hear together. See if you and your child can work out where the sound is coming from before the twins do, while having fun recreating the sounds for yourself at home.

This fun and colourful show further develops the young viewers ability to recognise and identify animals, reinforces colour identification and is a fun new way of learning. Get creative and host an animal toy party whilst you watch, or mess around and imitate the animal noises. No matter how you decide to interact with this wonderful show, the Happy Kingdom will always be full of fun.

programme.title: Children: Groups
programme.desc: Learning to categorise objects is so much easier with the help of the friendly baby fox in Groups. This show is most beneficial with sufficient interaction with the children that its aimed at, for example the learning of older children is enhanced by asking them questions such as "whats different" between two or more objects. For younger children it is more beneficial to just point out these differences or similarities. Groups helps to develop young viewers observational skills, attributing objects into different categories and recognising defining attributes of different objects.

programme.title: Children: In the Museum
programme.desc: Can you help Mr.Clown find the missing animals? When animals start mysteriously disappearing from some of the paintings in the museum, Mr.Clown must go searching for them so that he can put them back in their correct places. In the Museum is a great introduction to different kinds of art for the littlest viewers, promotes shape recognition and helps young viewers to recognise and identify different types of animals. Importantly you can also use the animals disappearing as a great way to let young viewers know that it is perfectly okay to make mistakes.

programme.title: Children: Home Sweet Home
programme.desc: This cartoon takes a look into the lives of a range of the cutest baby animals, and explores their family relationships. Everyday, after a big adventure exploring their surroundings, theyll return home to their loving families, to be greeted with lots of love and affection. As is the case with many Duck TV programmes, this programme is designed to both educate and entertain its young audience. Children will become able to recognise the similar characteristic features of animals, develop social skills, and present emotional bonds, as well as thoroughly enjoying their viewing time.

programme.title: Children: DuckSchool
programme.desc: In a forest kindergarden, woodland animals who call it their home are learning the basics of English from their helpful fairy teacher, Miss Sunshine. Learn some brand new words and practice your counting skills, or listen carefully to the stories Miss Sunshine has to tell. With Duckschool we can learn about how the seasons change, different kinds of weather, the amazing planets in our night sky and so many other things! There might even be some special guests to meet along the way.

programme.title: Children: Albert Explains
programme.desc: Albert the professor wants to show off all his skills and knowledge, and hopefully you can pick some of it up along the way, too! This programme is a Duck TV production, and is designed to be both informative and entertaining. The professor teaches his viewers cognitive skills and language skills, which they can apply to their everyday lives, too. He encourages children to categorise objects, growing their understanding for the objects, and also testing their skills of logic. The professor makes it fun and easy to follow, as he wants all his students to be happy while learning, creating a positive attitude towards personal growth and a passion for building new skills from a young age.

programme.title: Series: My Pet Family
programme.desc: Pets are part of the family! In My Pet Family, the preschooler Tony shows us how much joy, love and responsibility comes with owning pets. Molly, the cat and Lucas, the puppy give Tony all their love while they learn, play, eat, bath and share adventures together.Stories are backed by psychological research on how owning a pet is beneficial for children. While enjoying My Pet Family your children will receive support in understanding responsibilities and that animals are to be respected, protected and loved.

programme.title: Children: In the Museum
programme.desc: Can you help Mr.Clown find the missing animals? When animals start mysteriously disappearing from some of the paintings in the museum, Mr.Clown must go searching for them so that he can put them back in their correct places. In the Museum is a great introduction to different kinds of art for the littlest viewers, promotes shape recognition and helps young viewers to recognise and identify different types of animals. Importantly you can also use the animals disappearing as a great way to let young viewers know that it is perfectly okay to make mistakes.

programme.title: Series: My Pet Family
programme.desc: Pets are part of the family! In My Pet Family, the preschooler Tony shows us how much joy, love and responsibility comes with owning pets. Molly, the cat and Lucas, the puppy give Tony all their love while they learn, play, eat, bath and share adventures together.Stories are backed by psychological research on how owning a pet is beneficial for children. While enjoying My Pet Family your children will receive support in understanding responsibilities and that animals are to be respected, protected and loved.

programme.title: Children: Albert Explains
programme.desc: Albert the professor wants to show off all his skills and knowledge, and hopefully you can pick some of it up along the way, too! This programme is a Duck TV production, and is designed to be both informative and entertaining. The professor teaches his viewers cognitive skills and language skills, which they can apply to their everyday lives, too. He encourages children to categorise objects, growing their understanding for the objects, and also testing their skills of logic. The professor makes it fun and easy to follow, as he wants all his students to be happy while learning, creating a positive attitude towards personal growth and a passion for building new skills from a young age.

programme.title: Children: Home Sweet Home
programme.desc: This cartoon takes a look into the lives of a range of the cutest baby animals, and explores their family relationships. Everyday, after a big adventure exploring their surroundings, theyll return home to their loving families, to be greeted with lots of love and affection. As is the case with many Duck TV programmes, this programme is designed to both educate and entertain its young audience. Children will become able to recognise the similar characteristic features of animals, develop social skills, and present emotional bonds, as well as thoroughly enjoying their viewing time.

programme.title: Series: Dotty, the Kitty
programme.desc: A super fun and creative show, Dotty the Kitty attempts to connect the dots that the pencil draws to discover the hidden image and paint the final picture. As always with Duck TV this show make education and development exciting and enjoyable for its young viewers. Helping children to connect the dots improves their ability to recognise and identify shapes and objects, develop hand-eye coordination and for the slightly older viewers it improves their association of objects with their realistic shapes and colours. Encouraging the creativity and imagination out of your child, Dotty the Kitty provides endless fun!

programme.title: Children: Pixie 2
programme.desc: Join Lilali, the happy little purple-haired wizard elf, in his magical world. Lilai just loves to perform his magic tricks. This programme, for very young viewers, can help little ones learn basic vocabulary. Watch with children and repeat the words of the objects on the screen to teach them short, simple words. This short animation has been designed to help promote sound and object recognition and boost a childs cognitive skills. After you have watched the programme you can repeat the vocabulary from the programme whilst playing to reinforce the words learnt.

programme.title: Children: We Are Playing Now
programme.desc: Educational childrens magazine exploring the world around us, including familiar people and objects through drawing and painting. It helps children develop cognitive skills, as well as parent-child emotional relations, introducing them to different situations.

programme.title: Children: Tempo Giusto
programme.desc: Tempo Giusto is playful and fun introduction to the concept of time for young viewers. Lola and Henry work together as an excellent team. Whilst Lola uses her knowledge to tell the time, Henry, who is a wonderful storyteller, shows us what children get up to at different times of the day. This educational adventure teaches viewers a whole range of skills including the the sequencing of actions and some vital pre-math skills. Engaging with your little one about what they do at certain times of the day is a great way to bring Tempo Giusto to life!

programme.title: Children: Ducky and Fluffy
programme.desc: The Ducky family has a brand new member! With the arrival of her little brother Fluffy, Ducky experiences a wide range of new emotions and finds herself in new situations. Stories are created with the support of child psychologists to help children adjust to the arrival of a new sibling.

programme.title: Children: Margo And Felix
programme.desc: Margo and Felix live in a beautiful little house which they must take care of themselves. Although they are responsible for the maintenance of the house they also make lots of time to play games and have fun. Taking on the activities of both adults and children helps to start communication between children and parents about responsibility. Margo and Felix encourages creative thinking and lots of fun!

programme.title: Children: Henrys Stories
programme.desc: Henry loves telling stories, but he needs your help to make sure its all in the correct order. Follow Henry in these silent animated shorts as he constructs stories with the help of his handy picture cards. Narrate the sequences together and solve his picture puzzles to see the story come to life. Identify the beginnings and endings of simple everyday stories, while carefully piecing together all of the events in between. Teaches children about cause and effect, while encouraging logical thinking and deductive reasoning.

programme.title: Children: Ducky and Friends
programme.desc: In Ducky and Friends our little duck is sharing all the fun with her friends, Lola, Henry and Toby. Stories are created with the help of child psychologists and aim to teach toddlers how to play nicely with their friends without arguing and how to adapt during mutual play. They also show that exploring the world with peers brings joy and satisfaction.

programme.title: Series: Cubie
programme.desc: Animated childrens series following Cubie the builder who has fantastic plans for new buildings. Cubie loves to build and, with help from his friends, the cheerful cubes, erects inventive new constructions. With Cubie at the helm, the cubes know exactly what to do, and if they encounter a problem, Cubie is always there to help. This enjoyable series from Duck TV helps children build their spatial awareness and observational skills while learning about new prepositions and the basics of building.

programme.title: Children: Toby McFly
programme.desc: Toby McFly is a pilot dog, who shows us how the world looks from above. He is flying above beautiful nature scenery, animals, people and different places of interest. After admiring the view from above he lands his plane and shows us in detail what he saw from above.

programme.title: Children: Lola and the Numbers
programme.desc: Lola is a playful little girls who loves numbers! She is constantly on the move and is always ready to count together with her number firends from one to ten. Lola and the Numbers is all about setting that pre-math knowledge for its young viewers. The show helps us to identify different numbers, count from one to ten and develop our pre-math skills. The most important viewing tip is that we always count with Lola! whether in English or your own language, counting along is always fun!

programme.title: Series: Ducky Adventures
programme.desc: Every day is a different adventure for Ducky! This animated show for very young children lets toddlers and pre-schoolers to join Ducky and learn through daily activities. This series is brought to you by DuckTV, which works with child psychologists in creating programmes for babies and toddlers. Ducky Adventures has been designed to help your child develop their observational skills whilst also letting them use their imagination and creativity. This cartoon can be used as a conversation starter for the little ones in your life: you can talk to toddlers about their thoughts and opinions on the activities youve seen in the programme or the things that happen in your toddlers life.

programme.title: Children: DuckSchool
programme.desc: In a forest kindergarden, woodland animals who call it their home are learning the basics of English from their helpful fairy teacher, Miss Sunshine. Learn some brand new words and practice your counting skills, or listen carefully to the stories Miss Sunshine has to tell. With Duckschool we can learn about how the seasons change, different kinds of weather, the amazing planets in our night sky and so many other things! There might even be some special guests to meet along the way.

programme.title: Children: Sounds Around Us
programme.desc: Liza and Ben the little elf twins love learning about new sounds. Join them in this series of animated shorts to learn more about sounds, how to find them and how to recreate them. Follow them as they whizz away on exciting adventures together to investigate where different familiar sounds are coming from. Play along with the twins and encourage your child to listen and identify the sounds you hear together. See if you and your child can work out where the sound is coming from before the twins do, while having fun recreating the sounds for yourself at home.

programme.title: Children: Small – But Hardworking
programme.desc: This cartoon is designed to entertain and educate very young children, by showing three elves building a variety of different objects with materials such as wood and ice. Duck TV aims to produce content that is educational and aid the development of young children. This show effectively advances childrens ability to use their imagination, by stimulating their senses with a bright colourful cartoon, and the moving objects only enhances this further. The programme also aids children in beginning to recognise shapes, preparing them for school in doing so.

programme.title: Series: Ristorante
programme.desc: Welcome to the Ristorante, come in and find out all about how the restaurant works. Learn about all the different processes starting with the preparation and moving to the baking or the cooking, the serving and finally to the dish washing. Encourage your little ones to play pretend, cooking up some imaginary treats for you, your friends and family. Come along to Ristorante and youre sure to build up your vocabulary, whilst improving your ability to identify basic objects and their characteristics, and of course having fun!

programme.title: Children: Higher the Better
programme.desc: Join Kiteko, the goofy giraffe and Umi, the playful meerkat in Higher the Better, as they observe the everyday life of toddlers and learn from the children about their everyday activities such as picking apples and painting! When theyre not helping pick apples with the children, they are going on field trips and making lots of fun whilst they are playing. While watching, focus the attention of the youngster by speaking with them about what the children are drawing or how fast they can run! Combining education and fun, Higher the Better allows the development of social skills for toddlers, encourages them to observe and think deeper about what they are watching on their screen and initiates communication between parent and child, as well as children and their friends! Created by Ducktv, each animation, cartoon and mini-series is created with supervision of child psychologists to meet all the requirements of babies after three months of age. The combination between education, wholesome, amusing and relaxing elements within their shows aid toddlers to develop their visual and auditory abilities. Available 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, parents can be assured that their children can learn all the skills they need in life whilst still doing something fun!

programme.title: Children: Somewhere Over the Rainbow
programme.desc: Following the adventures of a brother and a sister. The siblings go over the rainbow to discover new worlds. In their travels they find out about many interesting things, including amazing animals, beautiful landscapes and more.

programme.title: Children: The Way We Travel
programme.desc: This cartoon is designed to aid the development of young children. Your child will watch various vehicles, therefore making them aware of a variety of different shapes and objects in the real world. They will also observe how they operate, which will allow them to grow an understanding of how they may be used in everyday life, as they see their different parts. Additionally, your child will experience the noises that these vehicles make, and be given the opportunity to acquire basic language skills, too. This show will not only keep young children entertained, but it will educate them too, in regards to the outside world.

programme.title: Children: Didy Baby
programme.desc: Didy Baby is a collection of fun and touching stories all about a group of adorable baby animals. The main theme of this heartwarming yet educational show is the idea of helping each other and working together. It aims to improve its young viewers social skills, develop their observational and thinking skills whilst introducing them to the concept of problem solving and decision making. The show consists of lots of simple situations and stories that encourage creative thinking and widen childrens awareness. As an added bonus, problem solving and story telling with your child will help to tighten your relationship.

Groups helps to develop young viewers observational skills, attributing objects into different categories and recognising defining attributes of different objects.

Engaging with your little one about what they do at certain times of the day is a great way to bring Tempo Giusto to life!

The group of friends are having lots of fun, and you are invited along. This is not only entertaining, but educational too. Duck TV productions aim to produce content to aid child development. This programme is designed to develop social skills and abilities, help young children learn new words in a creative way, identify new objects, and their use in everyday life.

programme.title: Children: Sport, Sport, Sport
programme.desc: Sport Sport Sport is all about, you guessed it, different types of sport. This fun animated show teaches us all about different kinds of exercises, physical activity and sports, promoting the benefits of being healthy and encouraging its young viewers to expand their hobbies by exploring new sports. For the littlest viewers, this sport-tastic show promotes motor skills and movement, increasing muscle strength and balance and helps to develop basic coordination. Learning about sport have never been easier or more exciting!

programme.title: Children: We Are Playing Now
programme.desc: Educational childrens magazine exploring the world around us, including familiar people and objects through drawing and painting. It helps children develop cognitive skills, as well as parent-child emotional relations, introducing them to different situations.

programme.title: Children: The Way We Travel
programme.desc: This cartoon is designed to aid the development of young children. Your child will watch various vehicles, therefore making them aware of a variety of different shapes and objects in the real world. They will also observe how they operate, which will allow them to grow an understanding of how they may be used in everyday life, as they see their different parts. Additionally, your child will experience the noises that these vehicles make, and be given the opportunity to acquire basic language skills, too. This show will not only keep young children entertained, but it will educate them too, in regards to the outside world.

programme.title: Series: Mimo and Bobo PLUS
programme.desc: Join the two familiar characters who have become preschoolers but still love fun adventures which teach them about various useful things. In their amazing adventures, Mimo and Bobo learn about friendship, sharing, helping others and more, helping children develop their social and observational skills.

programme.title: Children: Margo And Felix
programme.desc: Margo and Felix live in a beautiful little house which they must take care of themselves. Although they are responsible for the maintenance of the house they also make lots of time to play games and have fun. Taking on the activities of both adults and children helps to start communication between children and parents about responsibility. Margo and Felix encourages creative thinking and lots of fun!

programme.title: Children: Higher the Better
programme.desc: Join Kiteko, the goofy giraffe and Umi, the playful meerkat in Higher the Better, as they observe the everyday life of toddlers and learn from the children about their everyday activities such as picking apples and painting! When theyre not helping pick apples with the children, they are going on field trips and making lots of fun whilst they are playing. While watching, focus the attention of the youngster by speaking with them about what the children are drawing or how fast they can run! Combining education and fun, Higher the Better allows the development of social skills for toddlers, encourages them to observe and think deeper about what they are watching on their screen and initiates communication between parent and child, as well as children and their friends! Created by Ducktv, each animation, cartoon and mini-series is created with supervision of child psychologists to meet all the requirements of babies after three months of age. The combination between education, wholesome, amusing and relaxing elements within their shows aid toddlers to develop their visual and auditory abilities. Available 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, parents can be assured that their children can learn all the skills they need in life whilst still doing something fun!

programme.title: Children: Get Up!
programme.desc: If you are looking for a way to help your child develop their coordination and motor skills, look no further. Duck TV exercise presenters, Langi, Rundi, and Rendi, will guide your child through a simple step by step tutorial, which they can follow along at home. Its fun and easy, and gets kids up on their feet and moving. With all Duck TV productions, there is great educational benefits. This programme will develop a childs cognitive and motor skills, along with their coordination, which is essential to the development of a healthy child.

programme.title: Children: Happy Meadow
programme.desc: Two happy rabbits, Sari and Nati have lots of fun playing in Happy Meadow, in this childrens cartoon. They have plenty of other lovable friends who also live in Happy Meadow with them. This is a Duck TV production. Duck TV aim to produce content for young children that is educating, and aids their development, while being entertaining at the same time. programme.title: Children: Groups
programme.desc: Learning to categorise objects is so much easier with the help of the friendly baby fox in Groups. This show is most beneficial with sufficient interaction with the children that its aimed at, for example the learning of older children is enhanced by asking them questions such as "whats different" between two or more objects. For younger children it is more beneficial to just point out these differences or similarities. Groups helps to develop young viewers observational skills, attributing objects into different categories and recognising defining attributes of different objects.

programme.title: Series: Zack And Ziggy
programme.desc: This lovely animated childrens series explores the basic concepts of size and comparison. It follows the everyday adventures of a little nerdy boy named Zack and his loyal dog best friend, Ziggy. The inseparable pair turn every situation into a chance to learn, including taking a walk, playing sports and getting ready for bed. Join the two sweet friends on their exciting exploration of the world around them.

programme.title: Children: Albert Explains
programme.desc: Albert the professor wants to show off all his skills and knowledge, and hopefully you can pick some of it up along the way, too! This programme is a Duck TV production, and is designed to be both informative and entertaining. The professor teaches his viewers cognitive skills and language skills, which they can apply to their everyday lives, too. He encourages children to categorise objects, growing their understanding for the objects, and also testing their skills of logic. The professor makes it fun and easy to follow, as he wants all his students to be happy while learning, creating a positive attitude towards personal growth and a passion for building new skills from a young age.

The main theme of this heartwarming yet educational show is the idea of helping each other and working together. It aims to improve its young viewers social skills, develop their observational and thinking skills whilst introducing them to the concept of problem solving and decision making. The show consists of lots of simple situations and stories that encourage creative thinking and widen childrens awareness. As an added bonus, problem solving and story telling with your child will help to tighten your relationship.

programme.title: Children: Henrys Stories
programme.desc: Henry loves telling stories, but he needs your help to make sure its all in the correct order. Follow Henry in these silent animated shorts as he constructs stories with the help of his handy picture cards. Narrate the sequences together and solve his picture puzzles to see the story come to life. Identify the beginnings and endings of simple everyday stories, while carefully piecing together all of the events in between. Teaches children about cause and effect, while encouraging logical thinking and deductive reasoning.

programme.title: Children: DuckSchool
programme.desc: In a forest kindergarden, woodland animals who call it their home are learning the basics of English from their helpful fairy teacher, Miss Sunshine. Learn some brand new words and practice your counting skills, or listen carefully to the stories Miss Sunshine has to tell. With Duckschool we can learn about how the seasons change, different kinds of weather, the amazing planets in our night sky and so many other things! There might even be some special guests to meet along the way.

programme.title: Children: We Are Playing Now
programme.desc: Educational childrens magazine exploring the world around us, including familiar people and objects through drawing and painting. It helps children develop cognitive skills, as well as parent-child emotional relations, introducing them to different situations.

programme.title: Series: Dotty, the Kitty
programme.desc: A super fun and creative show, Dotty the Kitty attempts to connect the dots that the pencil draws to discover the hidden image and paint the final picture. As always with Duck TV this show make education and development exciting and enjoyable for its young viewers. Helping children to connect the dots improves their ability to recognise and identify shapes and objects, develop hand-eye coordination and for the slightly older viewers it improves their association of objects with their realistic shapes and colours. Encouraging the creativity and imagination out of your child, Dotty the Kitty provides endless fun!

programme.title: Children: Lola and the Numbers
programme.desc: Lola is a playful little girls who loves numbers! She is constantly on the move and is always ready to count together with her number firends from one to ten. Lola and the Numbers is all about setting that pre-math knowledge for its young viewers. The show helps us to identify different numbers, count from one to ten and develop our pre-math skills. The most important viewing tip is that we always count with Lola! whether in English or your own language, counting along is always fun!

programme.title: Children: Happy Kingdom
programme.desc: Happy Kingdom catches up with the adorable bunnies from Happy Meadow and introduces us to new friends like the princess Sari, the brave prince Nati, the caring cook-squirrel, the fearless knight-hedgehog and the resourceful wizard-bear. This fun and colourful show further develops the young viewers ability to recognise and identify animals, reinforces colour identification and is a fun new way of learning. Get creative and host an animal toy party whilst you watch, or mess around and imitate the animal noises. No matter how you decide to interact with this wonderful show, the Happy Kingdom will always be full of fun.

programme.title: Children: Sunville – Sportsville
programme.desc: All of your favourite Sunville residents join together to participate in one amazing sports day. Mister Goat, the Raccoon Family, Kitty Cat and the Friendly Pig are participating in Sports Day, and they want you to come along and join the fun! This interactive cartoon encourages children to join in and exercise alongside these incredibly cute characters, who can at times be a little competitive, too. In doing so, not only will your child have lots of fun, but they will be exercising and developing basic coordination skills along the way. They will also increase muscle strength and sense of balance, which will benefit them in their everyday lives, and keep them healthy and happy!

programme.title: Series: Cubie
programme.desc: Animated childrens series following Cubie the builder who has fantastic plans for new buildings. Cubie loves to build and, with help from his friends, the cheerful cubes, erects inventive new constructions. With Cubie at the helm, the cubes know exactly what to do, and if they encounter a problem, Cubie is always there to help. This enjoyable series from Duck TV helps children build their spatial awareness and observational skills while learning about new prepositions and the basics of building.

programme.title: Children: Toby McFly
programme.desc: Toby McFly is a pilot dog, who shows us how the world looks from above. He is flying above beautiful nature scenery, animals, people and different places of interest. After admiring the view from above he lands his plane and shows us in detail what he saw from above.

programme.title: Children: Lola and the Numbers

programme.title: Children: Get Up!
programme.desc: If you are looking for a way to help your child develop their coordination and motor skills, look no further. Duck TV exercise presenters, Langi, Rundi, and Rendi, will guide your child through a simple step by step tutorial, which they can follow along at home. Its fun and easy, and gets kids up on their feet and moving. With all Duck TV productions, there is great educational benefits. This programme will develop a childs cognitive and motor skills, along with their coordination, which is essential to the development of a healthy child.

programme.title: Children: Ducky and Friends
programme.desc: In Ducky and Friends our little duck is sharing all the fun with her friends, Lola, Henry and Toby. Stories are created with the help of child psychologists and aim to teach toddlers how to play nicely with their friends without arguing and how to adapt during mutual play. They also show that exploring the world with peers brings joy and satisfaction.

programme.title: Children: We Are Playing Now
programme.desc: Educational childrens magazine exploring the world around us, including familiar people and objects through drawing and painting. It helps children develop cognitive skills, as well as parent-child emotional relations, introducing them to different situations.

programme.title: Series: Ducky Adventures
programme.desc: Every day is a different adventure for Ducky! This animated show for very young children lets toddlers and pre-schoolers to join Ducky and learn through daily activities. This series is brought to you by DuckTV, which works with child psychologists in creating programmes for babies and toddlers. Ducky Adventures has been designed to help your child develop their observational skills whilst also letting them use their imagination and creativity. This cartoon can be used as a conversation starter for the little ones in your life: you can talk to toddlers about their thoughts and opinions on the activities youve seen in the programme or the things that happen in your toddlers life.

programme.title: Series: Ristorante
programme.desc: Welcome to the Ristorante, come in and find out all about how the restaurant works. Learn about all the different processes starting with the preparation and moving to the baking or the cooking, the serving and finally to the dish washing. Encourage your little ones to play pretend, cooking up some imaginary treats for you, your friends and family. Come along to Ristorante and youre sure to build up your vocabulary, whilst improving your ability to identify basic objects and their characteristics, and of course having fun!

programme.title: Children: Tempo Giusto
programme.desc: Tempo Giusto is a playful introduction to the understanding of the concept of time. The always cheerful Lola tells the time and together with the great storyteller Henry, they show us what kids do at different parts of the day.

programme.title: Children: Groups
programme.desc: Learning to categorise objects is so much easier with the help of the friendly baby fox in Groups. This show is most beneficial with sufficient interaction with the children that its aimed at, for example the learning of older children is enhanced by asking them questions such as "whats different" between two or more objects. For younger children it is more beneficial to just point out these differences or similarities. Groups helps to develop young viewers observational skills, attributing objects into different categories and recognising defining attributes of different objects.

programme.title: Children: Enlightment Corner
programme.desc: This cartoon, made for young children, is fun and entertaining, but also holds educational benefits. This is a Duck TV production, which aims to aid the development of children, in a fun and engaging way. This particular series will support a childs ability to identify everyday objects that they might encounter in their lives, learn new skills, and develop their thinking and observational skills, too. This programme makes learning fun and easy, so children pick up these skills in an effortless way, and remain engaged throughout. This is great way for children to learn, and a positive attitude towards gaining new skills will serve them well later on in life, too.

programme.title: Series: My Pet Family
programme.desc: Pets are part of the family! In My Pet Family, the preschooler Tony shows us how much joy, love and responsibility comes with owning pets. Molly, the cat and Lucas, the puppy give Tony all their love while they learn, play, eat, bath and share adventures together.Stories are backed by psychological research on how owning a pet is beneficial for children. While enjoying My Pet Family your children will receive support in understanding responsibilities and that animals are to be respected, protected and loved.

programme.title: Children: Pixie 2
programme.desc: Join Lilali, the happy little purple-haired wizard elf, in his magical world. Lilai just loves to perform his magic tricks. This programme, for very young viewers, can help little ones learn basic vocabulary. Watch with children and repeat the words of the objects on the screen to teach them short, simple words. This short animation has been designed to help promote sound and object recognition and boost a childs cognitive skills. After you have watched the programme you can repeat the vocabulary from the programme whilst playing to reinforce the words learnt.

programme.title: Children: In the Museum
programme.desc: Can you help Mr.Clown find the missing animals? When animals start mysteriously disappearing from some of the paintings in the museum, Mr.Clown must go searching for them so that he can put them back in their correct places. In the Museum is a great introduction to different kinds of art for the littlest viewers, promotes shape recognition and helps young viewers to recognise and identify different types of animals. Importantly you can also use the animals disappearing as a great way to let young viewers know that it is perfectly okay to make mistakes.

programme.title: Children: Home Sweet Home
programme.desc: This cartoon takes a look into the lives of a range of the cutest baby animals, and explores their family relationships. Everyday, after a big adventure exploring their surroundings, theyll return home to their loving families, to be greeted with lots of love and affection. As is the case with many Duck TV programmes, this programme is designed to both educate and entertain its young audience. Children will become able to recognise the similar characteristic features of animals, develop social skills, and present emotional bonds, as well as thoroughly enjoying their viewing time.

programme.title: Children: ABC – duckBC
programme.desc: Writing skills introduced, explained and developed through the animated adventures of the five stalwarts of the art of penmanship: Pen, Pencil, Stamp, Eraser and Brush. From A to Z, the five friends take children through the steps to produce beautiful letters and write wonderful words.

programme.title: Children: Sunville
programme.desc: Your favourite residents of Sunville: Mister Goat, the Dog, Racoon Family, KittyCat, the Friendly Pig give you an insight into their everyday lives. The group of friends are having lots of fun, and you are invited along. This is not only entertaining, but educational too. Duck TV productions aim to produce content to aid child development. This programme is designed to develop social skills and abilities, help young children learn new words in a creative way, identify new objects, and their use in everyday life.

programme.title: Series: Ristorante
programme.desc: Welcome to the Ristorante, come in and find out all about how the restaurant works. Learn about all the different processes starting with the preparation and moving to the baking or the cooking, the serving and finally to the dish washing. Encourage your little ones to play pretend, cooking up some imaginary treats for you, your friends and family. Come along to Ristorante and youre sure to build up your vocabulary, whilst improving your ability to identify basic objects and their characteristics, and of course having fun!

programme.title: Children: Tempo Giusto
programme.desc: Tempo Giusto is a playful introduction to the understanding of the concept of time. The always cheerful Lola tells the time and together with the great storyteller Henry, they show us what kids do at different parts of the day.

programme.title: Series: Cubie
programme.desc: Animated childrens series following Cubie the builder who has fantastic plans for new buildings. Cubie loves to build and, with help from his friends, the cheerful cubes, erects inventive new constructions. With Cubie at the helm, the cubes know exactly what to do, and if they encounter a problem, Cubie is always there to help. This enjoyable series from Duck TV helps children build their spatial awareness and observational skills while learning about new prepositions and the basics of building.

programme.title: Children: Didy Baby
programme.desc: Didy Baby is a collection of fun and touching stories all about a group of adorable baby animals. The main theme of this heartwarming yet educational show is the idea of helping each other and working together. It aims to improve its young viewers social skills, develop their observational and thinking skills whilst introducing them to the concept of problem solving and decision making. The show consists of lots of simple situations and stories that encourage creative thinking and widen childrens awareness. As an added bonus, problem solving and story telling with your child will help to tighten your relationship.

programme.title: Children: Doll Team to the Rescue
programme.desc: Join Bell and her friends Fido the Kangaroo and Lilo the Bear as they come to help everyone and anyone in the forest! Incorporating education into enjoyable animations, cartoons and mini-series, Doll Team to the Rescue educates toddlers and children in developing their social skills with others, the importance of friendship, all whilst being able to experience various adventures! The main message within Doll Team to the Rescue is to teach children the love and respect for animals. Ducktv recommend that parents, in order to teach the importance of taking care of people as well as respecting animals, should take them to an animal shelter and explain the necessity of protecting and rescuing animals. Ducktv which specialises in television for absolute beginners create animations, cartoons and miniseries bring fun alongside entertainment for the smallest TV viewers. Under supervision of child psychologists in order to meet all requirements for babies after 3 months, the characteristics of each episode of their shows with music help children to develop their cognitive capabilities. Available 24 hours and 7 days a week, Ducktv ensures to amuse, develop and relax younger audiences as well as educating them in an enjoyable way!

programme.desc: Following the adventures of a curious little dino boy in the Mesosoic era, as he discovers the world around him. Join Milo and his friends and family to find out how dinosaurs lived. The programme helps little children develop their social skills, as well as their imagination, introducing them to the era of dinosaurs.

programme.title: Children: Henrys Stories
programme.desc: Henry loves telling stories, but he needs your help to make sure its all in the correct order. Follow Henry in these silent animated shorts as he constructs stories with the help of his handy picture cards. Narrate the sequences together and solve his picture puzzles to see the story come to life. Identify the beginnings and endings of simple everyday stories, while carefully piecing together all of the events in between. Teaches children about cause and effect, while encouraging logical thinking and deductive reasoning.

programme.title: Children: Happy Kingdom
programme.desc: Happy Kingdom catches up with the adorable bunnies from Happy Meadow and introduces us to new friends like the princess Sari, the brave prince Nati, the caring cook-squirrel, the fearless knight-hedgehog and the resourceful wizard-bear. This fun and colourful show further develops the young viewers ability to recognise and identify animals, reinforces colour identification and is a fun new way of learning. Get creative and host an animal toy party whilst you watch, or mess around and imitate the animal noises. No matter how you decide to interact with this wonderful show, the Happy Kingdom will always be full of fun.

programme.title: Children: Groups
programme.desc: Learning to categorise objects is so much easier with the help of the friendly baby fox in Groups. This series explores the different concepts being used to help sustain our future, such as alternative resources, biodiversity conservation and the future of travel.

programme.title: Info: The 77 Percent
programme.desc: 77 per cent of Africas population are below the age of thirty-five yet their interests are under-represented poltically and economically. This show aims to redress the balance by providing a voice to the largest demographic group on the continent. These dynamic younger people are politically engaged and will determine the future path their countries, and the continent as a whole, will follow in the twenty-first century. Presented by Eddy Micah Jr. from Ghana and Wanjiku Mwaura from Kenya, the show promotes a pan-African agenda by encouraging dialogue between the various interested parties. The show pulls no punches when delivering its compelling reports, personal accounts and provocative discussions. A long overdue look at the big issues that affect the youth of Africa.

programme.title: Info: Odyssey of the Orphans – The Plight of Children After World War II – Part 2
programme.desc: The Second World War claimed the lives of millions of people and left many children orphaned. One of the worst-affected countries was Poland, where entire families were wiped out. This documentary highlights the desperate fate of these children orphaned by war.

programme.title: Info: Close Quarter Battle
programme.desc: The Bosnian War was an extraordinarily complex event, with many layers of military involvement including NATO forces, national militaries, irregular paramilitary forces, mujahedeen revolutionaries, private security companies, and international intelligence personnel. One tactic in particular struck fear into the hearts of the military and civilians alike: the use of snipers positioned in high buildings. This edition of CQB investigates this speciﬁ c combat technique and how it was countered by opposing forces. Taking viewers inside a "snipers den," the program explains how this tactic was so successfully used by rebel forces-and how traditional military techniques evolved to combat it.

programme.title: Info: What In the World
programme.desc: Presented by Peadar King, this series illustrates the human consequences of global economic inequalities and human rights violations, by focusing on how people encounter these issues on a daily basis. At the heart of Africa, the Congo for many people will always be associated with Joseph Conrads early twentieth-century novel the Heart of Darkness, a title that has become a by-word for the country. And for Benjamin and David, two former child soldiers, and Funaha held as a sex slave by one of the many militias that continue to terrorise the country, that metaphor remains a daily reality. The film explores how this seemingly never-ending conflict impacts on the people of North Kivu.

programme.title: Info: Past Hunters
programme.desc: Built in the early 1800s, Whitby Hall used to be an administrative center and now stands as a public park and arts center. It has never before been investigated, but staff have reported many noises and presences among them.

programme.title: Info: Past Hunters
programme.desc: The county of Flintshire in Wales is said to be a land filled with ghosts and haunts. Plas Teg is said to be one of the "most haunted" houses in the area. With over 400 years of history, this place is sure to be the home of many an entity.

programme.title: Info: Rip Files

Also, well swim with real mermaids at Weeki Wachee Springs in Central Florida, and cheer on Teddy Ballgame at the Ted Williams Hitters Hall of Fame.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Journeys in Africa
programme.desc: To this day sisal, a rope making fiber plant, is a mainstay of the economy. Journeys tours the capital city of Tanzania and its diverse religious institutions before heading into sisal country. Well learn about the German influences and the seldom heard story of Livingstones final trip across Africa.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Journeys in Africa
programme.desc: This is one of the few national parks in Africa where the bush meets the ocean. The big game of Africa face off with the creatures of the deep. Our host goes a little rogue for supper and tries his hand at surf netting prawns after spending a day looking for the elusive elephants of Saadani.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Around the World in 80 Islands
programme.desc: A trip to Sardinia, along the western coast, to the Sinis protected marine area and the Island of Mal di Ventre. Together with Angelo, a local diving instructor, we dive around the Catalano rocks where we swim between the basaltic columns, arches and huge eroded volcanic rocks. Back on land we visit the strange architecture of San Giovanni del Sinis and the famous historic archeological site of Tharros, one of the largest ancient cities in the Mediterranean, founded by Phoenicians and inhabited for 1900 years. We then visit the Mistras lagoon where we see thousands of Flamingos and Cormorants, and it is here that we find Giuseppes riding stables, where he has a center for traditional horse training which is the art of "Monta da Lavoro". And talking of tradition, we end our Sardinian journey with a close-up on Sardinian traditions, local arts and crafts, food and folklore.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Around the World in 80 Islands
programme.desc: In the middle of the Indian Ocean, 2000 kilometres from the east coast of Africa, 800 east of Madagascar, and 220 north-east of Reunion, is the island of Mauritius, a volcanic island where different races, cultures, religions, colours and spices all live together in harmony. We visit the Ile Aix Aigrettes, a nature reserve that protects rare and interesting species such as the pink pigeon, giant tortoises, orchids and native lizards. This small island is the jewel in the crown of the Mauritius Wildlife Foundation that works for the protection of every animal and all of the vegetation in the territory. The entrance fee to the island contributes to financing the Foundations projects. Working our way south-west of the island we see the Tamarind Falls and the Le Morne Penisula, where people come from all over the world to kite surf.

programme.title: Info: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: Were shipping off to Belfast, Northern Ireland on todays episode. First, well gawk at the worlds biggest Titanic museum. Then, well learn about the provinces complicated history at the Ulster Museum. Finally, we get thrown in the slammer at the very creepy, Crumlin Road Jail.

programme.title: Info: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: Bonjour! Were headed to Quebec Province on todays show. First, we get blown away by the thunderous pipes at Montreals Notre Dame Basilica. After that, we go underneath the city at the Pointe a Calliere archaeology museum. Next, well learn about the native ecosystem at the gigantic, indoor, BioDome. Lastly, well learn about the 1967 Montreal Expo at the structures that are still visited today.

programme.title: Info: Out Of Town Adventures
programme.desc: Outta Town Adventures travels both near and far to discover the best advenures the destinations have to offer. Season 1 visits attractions from California to Rwanda, Switzerland, Iceland, Utah, Zambia, Mexico, The Grand Canyon, Georgia (the Eastern European one) Louisiana, Hawaii, Mauritius and Seychelles. This TV series is dedicated to presenting history, culture and geography in a fun and pisitive way. It encourages people to explore this beautiful world – something that starts with simply getting out of town!

programme.desc: In this episode we meet the Vorarlberg province in Austria. Characteristic of the area is the rural landscape, with farms and large houses made of rustic wood.

programme.title: Info: New Frontier
programme.desc: It has fired our imaginations for millennia, Mars, the God of War and the source of Mans science fictional demise. We know the dry barren planet was once flowing with vast reservoirs of water, the sky thick and filled with clouds and the tantalizing possibility of life. It is the only other place in our solar system than Man might one day call home.

programme.title: Info: New Frontier
programme.desc: From the beginnings of our Solar System four and half billion years ago there remains tantalizing clues to its evolution; remnent debris: asteroids and comets. They vary in size from grains of dust to mountain sides, footballs to planetoids. They were the building blocks of the planets and perhaps carry the origins of life itself. Now within our grasp these rocks of ice and dust are ready to give up their secrets.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: On the Cities Rooftops
programme.desc: How is life on the citys roofs? This series scales new heights, exploring apartment buildings, towers and monuments to discover a world full of unsuspected treasures : our rooftops. By day and night, the population changes on these heights. There are people who work here, people who live here, and others who come here to relax. The worlds rooftops are a continual hive of activity…

programme.title: Info: Wow, I Never Knew That!
programme.desc: On a hot summers day, nothing cools you down like a frozen fruity POPSICLE! Youll learn how an 11-year old boy created this sweet icy treat! And, have you ever noticed those colored spinning poles outside the BARBERSHOP? Youll be in STITCHES when you learn how they got their start! Plus, find out how a melting chocolate bar gave way to the invention of the MICROWAVE!

programme.title: Info: Wow, I Never Knew That!
programme.desc: Its the city of love, Paris, France. The world over knows its most famous structure, the Eiffel Tower! But did you know PARISIANS originally wanted to tear it down! Well explain why and how it was saved! Then, youll visit Americas FIRST PIZZERIA! And how the gourmet ice cream HAAGEN DAZS got its exotic start in Bronx New York!

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Water: H2O Stories
programme.desc: Water: H2O Stories is a 3x52 series revisiting the story of water on planet Earth and its disrupted course over time which has led to the 21st century biggest challenge.

programme.title: Info: Blue Realm
programme.desc: Filmed using crystal clear High Definition technology, The Blue Realm takes the viewer on a fascinating and breath-taking journey of discovery beneath the waves to examine the unique biology and extraordinary behaviour of undersea animals. Filmed by expert divers with a passion for marine life and environment, the compelling stories and captivating creatures come from many locations around the world including Papua New Guinea, Palau, South Africa, the Red Sea, the Great Barrier Reef, the Bahamas, Cocos Island, British Columbia, Texas, Indonesia, the Socorro Archipelago, California and Florida.

programme.desc: The vast expanse of space continues to hold our adventurous gaze. With each passing year we learn more about what truly lies beyond our planet and, with the advancement of technology, our progress is exponential. This documentary series examines our findings thus far, revealing the secrets we have learned and the mysteries we have unravelled. But there are many more questions waiting for us to answer..

programme.title: Nature + Travels: A Year in the Wild
programme.desc: As a new year starts in the heart of Africa, the rainy season has come to the Okavango Delta in Botswana, and with it begins a season of plenty and the luxury of permanent and abundant water sources. In South Africas Hluhluwe-Imfolozi Game Reserve, a group of rare samango monkeys take advantage of the abundant fruit born by a large Natal fig tree. In Thailand, a group of rhesus macaques have discovered a mango tree, and are busy feeding and stuffing their throat pouches with the fruit. Back in the Okavango Delta, the rains have also brought large buffalo herds back to the Xakanaxa area, the territory of a powerful pride of lions. Life and death are also a close-run thing for young gannet fledglings on their massive breeding colony of 50.000 birds on Malgas Island off the South African coast. As the young birds attempt to spread their wings and take to the air, some end up in the water. Many young animals have to run a gauntlet early on in life, and as a young loggerhead turtle hatches out of its egg and emerges from the sand on a beach in Mozambique, it faces a gruelling journey from its nest on the beach down to the sea. African penguins, too, are adapted to life at sea, but rest

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Sarah Shark
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Sarah Shark
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: Ray starts by hitching a lift on a research crane to get a birds eye view over the Rainforest; from there, he can see the geographical position responsible for this lush vegetation: mountain range in the west and the sea in the east. He then goes down to the ground, delving into the heart of the jungle, he comes across millennial trees, camouflage spiders and a miniature dinosaur, the Boyds Forest Dragon. He pursues his journey by travelling on a zipwire with wildlife expert, Justin McMahon. Together they observe life in the canopy. Meanwhile, Rays cameraman Martin Hayward Smith has been filming an animal that can only be found in this part of the world: the Bennetts tree kangaroo, a cute marsupial that lives like a monkey.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: Ray takes the Great Ocean Road along the Antarctic facing coast of Australia – the longest South facing coastline in the world. He starts in Port Philp Bay the entrance to Melbourne Harbour where for the first time he sees a strange marine creature – the weedy sea dragon – a relative of the sea horse. He also swims with a unique species of dolphin – the Burrunan Dolphins.Crossing the Bay he heads off down the longest War Memorial in the world – the Great Ocean Road and meets 93 year old Doug Stirling who remembers the world war 1 veterans building the road.Ray visits the Penguin Colony on Middle Island where guard dogs protect the penguins from foxes and he watches the night time return of the penguins after a day spent at sea fishing.He takes to the seas and discovers the creatures of the deep waters – albatross, balls of krill and a pod of fast moving common dolphins.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: In this episode, Ray explores the Red Centre of the country and shows that the Australian desert is filled with life for those who know where to find water.He arrives in the Red Centre by chopper as he flies over the Uluru monolith or Ayres Rock. For his first stop, he goes to a red kangaroo sanctuary where he cuddles a joey, meets their carer Brolga and gets close to the usually wary adult red kangaroos. He pursues his journey deeper in the desert to meet a local aboriginal Sammy Wilson. They go to a traditional waterhole and chat over a camp fire about Sammys ancestral knowledge of the land. Ray spends the night out under the stars before driving more inland to rocky areas where water collects. There Ray comes face to face with a wild kangaroo and rock wallabies. He then follows tracks along a dry river bed that lead him to Australias wild dog: a dingo.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Animal Embassy
programme.desc: The dilemma faced by every 21st Century wildlife park is how to attract and educate the public, while maintaining first class conditions for its inhabitants and leading the way in scientific research and environmental protection. Tucked away in the Canary Islands, one zoo is providing a masterclass in the art. For the past 2 years running, Loro Parque has been voted "The Worlds Best Zoo" by subscribers of Trip Advisor, echoing the highest possible accreditations of animal welfare, conservation and environmental bodies across the globe. It is now considered more popular than the prestigious San Diego, Singapore, ZooParc de Beauval, Prague, Chester and St.Louis Zoos. So how has a privately-owned zoo in a Spanish colony off the West coast of Africa earned such recognition? How does it balance the meticulous care and presentation of thousands of species, with the multi-million-dollar research and conservation programs dedicated to saving many of them from extinction? Whats the strategy behind its educational commitment to turning every pleasure-seeking tourist into a die-hard environmentalist? And who manages the harvest of tonnes of organic fruit needed to feed the animals d

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Animal Embassy
programme.desc: Federica the turtle has arrived from Italy after a run in with a container ship. Loro Parques offered to be her forever home, but how will she go sharing her new digs with others? Youve heard of a fish out of water – try a turtle! Esmeralda the iguana has a lumpy belly and Jorge the vet is worried. Hes hoping its a bounty of eggs but knows he shouldnt count his iguanas before they hatch. Its fingers crossed for some scaly babies!

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Herding Sheep In Iceland
programme.desc: Starting at the beginning of September, the Northern Lights unveil their magical patterns on Icelands starry skies. At the same time, Icelanders celebrate the "Retir": sheep and horses are herded to the lowlands. 4,500 sheep and 800 horses spend 3 to 4 months in the untamed highlands. Now, they are rounded up. No single farmer can herd so many animals to the lowlands. The entire community helps.

programme.title: Info: Deep Blue Dive
programme.desc: The ethos of freediving is simple. The challenge: to dive as deep as possible on just one breath. The drive: to explore the ocean in the purest way. The goal: to make it back to the surface in a coherent state. In "Deep Blue Dive" we voyage into this deep and dangerous world with Trevor Hutton, a freediver from South Africa, and reveal the extraordinary physiological challenges which have to be overcome to succeed in this sport. Trevor is a self-taught freediver operating on the periphery of the sport; southern Africa is not a chosen freediving location for good reason. The coastline is hostile, the swell runs high and the deeper water is frequented by every dangerous species of shark imaginable, the Great White in particular. Trevor is six feet tall and he weighs 220 pounds. This is a heavy frame to supply with oxygen, but hes well equipped. His lung capacity is nine litres and his average heart rate is 43 beats per minute. As soon as he hits the water, a set of strange physiological phenomena take over. We see how nerve receptors in his face trigger a response in the heart – slowing it down by an incredible 50%. Simultaneously, blood vessels in the skin and outer reaches of his

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Life in the Blue
programme.desc: This films reveals the extraordinary variety of life found in the vast blue expanses of te open ocean. Here, all the action takes place in a 10 metre deep band of water, just under the surface. Many species use this section of water to migrate and hunt while others use ingenious ways to stay hidden where there appears to be no shelter. From the surface, the huge blue expanses of the open ocean appear to be devoid of all life. Popular belief is that most sea life congregates around mainline coasts, islands or rocky outcrops. But that perception is far from the truth. This 4K film,shot in the Atlantic, reveals the extraordinary diversity of species who call the open ocean their home and the tactics they use to survive in the watery wilderness. Most of the life here congregates in a nutrient-rich band of water, around 10 metres from the surface. But it is brutal life out in the open ocean. There is little shelter, big predators abound and food is hard to find. Only those who adapt to the conditions have a hope of surviving in the blue void. Barracuda are a common species in the open water and they travel in large spiraling groups close the surface as a defense mechanism against bigger

programme.title: Info: Mongolia, Steppes Emirate
programme.desc: Battered by strong winds, and seen as a grazing land, Mongolia is the kingdom of steppes. With important mineral resources such as copper or uranium, coal and rare soil, Mongolia future is secure: the economy shows a significant growth rate and it is a business paradise for some expatriates. But for most of the population, needs remain unfulfilled.

programme.title: Info: What In the World
programme.desc: Presented by Peadar King, this series illustrates the human consequences of global economic inequalities and human rights violations, by focusing on how people encounter these issues on a daily basis. At the heart of Africa, the Congo for many people will always be associated with Joseph Conrads early twentieth-century novel the Heart of Darkness, a title that has become a by-word for the country. And for Benjamin and David, two former child soldiers, and Funaha held as a sex slave by one of the many militias that continue to terrorise the country, that metaphor remains a daily reality. The film explores how this seemingly never-ending conflict impacts on the people of North Kivu.

programme.title: Info: Music Voyager
programme.desc: Music Voyager is a music and travel broadcast series (television/cable, broadband, in-flight and mobile) that invites viewers to discover the exciting sounds of the planet. The host is Jacob Edgar, an explorer who does not search for lost cities or ancient ruins. Hes on the quest for a different kind of treasure…music. As an ethnomusicologist and world music record producer, Edgar travels the globe hunting for the best songs the world has to offer, and he suffers through some of the worst…so you dont have to. Along the way, hes rewarded with a backstage pass to concert halls, street festivals, recording studios and rehearsal rooms. With local musicians as his guide, Edgar tastes exotic and occasionally ghastly food, visits off-the-beaten path attractions and parties the night away to amazing concerts at hidden venues that only the locals know. Join music voyager for unexpected adventures and surprising discoveries that unveil the magic, mystery and music of far off lands.

programme.title: Info: Close Quarter Battle
programme.desc: The practice of hiring private armies goes back to ancient times, and the mystique associated with the mercenary warrior has been the subject of many historical studies and ﬁ ctional characterizations. This episode of CQB takes a more contemporary look at a day in the life of a group of civilian contractors, and how their role has evolved on the modern battleﬁ eld. Using its "sub-second" analysis techniques and intimate ﬁrst-person footage, CQB reveals the backgrounds, training and equipment of todays "soldiers for hire" and how private armies are re-shaping the way conﬂ icts are conducted around the world.

programme.title: Info: Past Hunters
programme.desc: Carnfield Hall is a country house dating from the 15th and 16th Centuries. This private residence turn event hall is using its paranormal activity to draw in business. Are these spirits the old residents?

programme.title: Info: Past Hunters
programme.desc: The team investigate a disused factory in Burton-Upon-Trent. Reports of paranormal happenings are common and the team are ready for anything.

programme.title: Info: Rip Files
programme.desc: Hill View Manor is filled with restless spirits who have no where else to go. Can the team connect with them?

programme.title: Info: Rip Files
programme.desc: The team explores St. Albans, a former sanitarium, and captures several shocking EVPs (spirit voices), including the one that became the title of this episode.

programme.title: Info: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: O Say can you see? Were in Baltimore, MD. Well learn about the Battle of Baltimore at Fort McHenry and the inspiration of the Star Spangled Banner. Then we dig deep into the history of Baltimores most famous resident, Edgar Allan Poe. Well sift through a huge collection of pop art and collectibles at the Geppi Museum, and learn about cracking codes at the National Cryptology museum.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Journeys in Africa
programme.desc: This is one of the few national parks in Africa where the bush meets the ocean. The big game of Africa face off with the creatures of the deep. Our host goes a little rogue for supper and tries his hand at surf netting prawns after spending a day looking for the elusive elephants of Saadani.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Journeys in Africa
programme.desc: If there ever was a lost wildlife gem, it would be Mikumi. Here many of the Big Twelve live their lives against the backdrop of one of the most scenic parks in Africa. Bill takes a break from the wildlife safari to investigate the huge salt works at the edge of the park and how it may impact future conservation.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Around the World in 80 Islands
programme.desc: Our destination is the island of Rodrigues, in the Mascarene archipelago, a volcanic folly that is only 109 square kilometres surrounded by an uncontaminated coral reef. We visit the island and discover its beauty on land, underground and also underwater. In the Francois Leguat protected reserve we are privileged to see hundreds of Tortoises, a varying ages and sizes, as they mate undisturbed by our presence and our cameras. A local guide takes us to discover a system of caves that develops 18 metres below sea level. But it is the population of Rodriguez that surprises us the most: A people who have not adopted different ways or customs, but that live their lives proudly with the knowledge that they are fortunate to have been born in such an island paradise both on land and sea.

programme.title: Nature + Travels: Around the World in 80 Islands
programme.desc: An adventure in Croatia, to discover the Adriatic Sea but in apnoea. Together with Mike Maric, born in Rovigno dIstria and world record holder in apnoea, we explore the underwater sea beds, small very green islands and picturesque towns. But above all we visit the Brionian archipelago, and a National Park, of rare beauty, that in a very special way unites nature and different animal species and unexpected vegetables. Underwater, in apnoea, we swim over a field of Pinna nobilis or Noble Pen Shells, we enter underwater tunnels and caves with their magical light beams and finally we visit, at about 28 to 40 metres underwater the "Baron Gautch" a steam-boat that was shipwrecked in 1914, which is still quite well preserved.

programme.title: Info: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: We travel to the end of the rainbow in Dublin, Ireland. Well gawk at the Book of Kells, a holy book displayed at Trinity College. We visited the hallowed halls of St. Patricks Cathedral, and touched famed Irishman, Daniel OConnells crypt at Glasnevin Cemetery. Finally, we learn the complicated history of Irish independence at Kilmainham jail.

programme.title: Info: Travel Thru History
programme.desc: This episode we visit the bright lights of Vancouver, Canada. Well swing along the famous Capilano Suspension Bridge, get tranquil in Dr. Sun Yat Sens Chinese garden, learn about Captain Vancouver at the Vancouver Maritime Museum, dig up Cesna Em "The City Before the City" at the Museum of Vancouver, and dive into the citys seedy underbelly at the Police Museum.
